newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to scrap reserve requirements lower limits.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to scrap reserve requirements lower limits.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling and opposition lawmakers have agreed to scrap the lower limits of banks' reserve requirements, deputy central banker Hsu Chia-tung told reporters on Monday.
"Lawmakers have reached the consensus to uphold the upper limits of banks' reserve requirements and scrap the lower limits," Hsu said.
The decision, which will require revising the Central Bank Law, needs approval from the full parliament.
The latest agreement was a compromise between the central bank and lawmakers, Hsu said.
The central bank had proposed scrapping the specified range limits altogether to improve Taiwan's bid to join the World Trade Organisation.
But a legislative joint committee proposed on March 18 to set the legal range of reserve requirements for cheque deposits at five percent to 25 percent, down from 15-40 percent.

The committee's proposed legal range for passbook deposits was at 5-25 percent from 10-35 percent, while that for saving deposits was at 3-15 percent from 5-20 percent. The proposed range for time deposits was at 3-15 percent from 7-25 percent.
Hsu told reporters on Monday the bank had no plans to discuss lowering banks' reserve requirements during its upcoming May 8 board meeting.
